questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Wanted to experience Berlin with its culture and history. The University also offered courses that I am interested in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Loved it! 
Only downside it the timing of the semester (April-July). Other than that, the city is amazing and the classes were good.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. But show up at orientation!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Tour of campus, orientation etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was good.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used WGgesucht, which works well. You can make a profile and find a lot of places that look for a roommate or an apartment by yourself. But you have to write to a lot of people. I lived two different places during the semester, so you might have to bee ready to move around a bit. Besides that I would recommend finding a place off campus - compared to Copenhagen, its still a lot more accesible.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its the best way to experience the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The people I spoke to who lived in student houses were not very satisfied.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy enough.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
We could try out courses for the first few weeks, then do a final registration. 
When applying for pre-approval, you can find the old courses from the previous year (e.g if you are going in summer 2025, check list of courses for summer 2024), they often offer a lot of the same courses. Necessary as the new list of courses is published later than you have to apply for pre-approval (when I went).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Easy to get in touch with the university, they were very helpful if there were any doubts.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I got all the classes I wanted.
Note that seminars are hard to get: Limited spaces and you have to preregister. So if you know you want to do a seminar, check which ones are offered and how to pre-register (often you have to write an email to the professor to sign up for a lottery to get a spot at the seminar).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are not doing seminars, do not stress too much. All other courses are easy to get a spot in. Try out some courses the first week and see what you like.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Found the courses interesting and challenging. You do 5 courses if you need 30 ECTS. There a tutorials and lectures in most of the regular courses, very similar to KU. Make sure you you prepare for exams during the semester as most exams start right after teaching is over and many are in the same week.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Fairly similar to KU, but variation between courses. Exams were in some regards more tough than at KU as you had less time to prepare and study for them and many were only 1,5-2 hours and all written by hand.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Similar style.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Empirical Development Economics, European Economic History 1918-, Advanced Monetary Economics, Public Economics, and Wealth Inequality (seminar)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Empirical Development Economics and European Economic History. Especially the first one was great if you are interested in the field.
(just a heads up: the exam in Public economics was insane even though the course seemed pretty straightforward).

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
You pay a semester fee where all transportation is included (which is super nice).
Not sure otherwise.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping (and beer and cigarettes) was a lot cheaper than i expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Great opportunities to do sports very cheaply through the university. Lots of social activities through whatsapp groups as well. Teachers and students also host talks and open seminars. 
You can also do a language course before the semester starts - something i regret not signing up for!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Explore the city (see as much as you can - get a bicycle!). Sign up for sports (nice way to feel at home in my opinion). Drink beers at a späti (its cheap and fun). 
Sign up for the campus tour! You will meet other people on exchange but from other fields of study.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the nearby lakes - generally explore the surroundings of Berlin. Go out. Tempelhof (Schiellerkiez). Go for a long bike ride. Eat at Kimchi Princess. Go to a park and enjoy all the green spaces. Eat cheap durums.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. People are really sweet.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to them after class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Would have loved to practice my german more before I went, but not a big problem. Culturally its not so different from DK/KBH, just more open.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Not sure, just the atmosphere.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go for as long as you can, you will feel like its over so fast. Have visitors, but NOT every weekend, take your time to enjoy it on your own terms and have time to spend with new people. Get a bike and go everywhere on it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare a little for your exams along the way so most of your summer is not spent inside :) (ask for advice for local students, they are really sweet and helpful).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Accepting being stuck inside at the height of summer..

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
